newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends flat on central bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends flat on central bank intervention.

text.p: The won ended Friday's trading flat against the opening after players were cautioned by active central Bank of Korea intervention, traders said.
The central bank has refused to comment on talk of its intervention on the interbank market.
After a failed early morning attempt to slow the won's fall by offering to sell dollars in forward trading, the central bank stepped into the spot market.
It sold dollars twice when the won fell to the 870 level.
The won closed the day at 869.60. It moved in a tight 869-870 range.
The won will see some short-term support next week as off-shore funds are expected to sell about $600-$700 million.
"But that is just a drop in the bucket compared to the dollar demand there is for import settlements," said a foreign bank dealer.
South Korea's widening trade deficit and the dollar's bullish trend against the Japanese yen will continue to pressure the won, traders said.
On Monday, the won was expected to move in a similar 869-870 range, they said. The base mid-rate was seen pegged at 869.50, compared to Friday's 869.00.
